purpose: Audit city-scoped land/cadastre evidence separately from accessible public parcel geometry; record only executed searches and actual page/request outcomes.
name: Banjul
pointBasis: Chosen approximate central-city query point; not a WUP centroid or official boundary.
jurisdiction: City of Banjul is within the mapped Greater Banjul area; national land policy and registry fall under the Ministry of Lands, Regional Government and Religious Affairs.
registryBasis: Ministry of Lands is the national land administration authority. The 2024 Auditor General review says Greater Banjul areas have cadastral mapping, while also describing gaps in functional GIS and digitized geographic referencing. This is city-region cadastre evidence, not a public geometry service.
findings: Direct inspection of the Gambia National Audit Office’s 2023 land-registration audit confirms that cadastral maps exist for the Greater Banjul Area, which includes Banjul, but that only parts of the country are cadastrally mapped. The same audit reports the geographical-referencing system is underdeveloped, land records are mostly paper-based, and there is no public digital access. The documented map is not a public parcel-vector service.
